title: Skool & Circle.so Alternative in India 2026: Prices Checked
description: Running a paid study community in India? Skool and Circle.so's US-dollar plans and fees next to rupee options with UPI, live classes and tests, and when to stay put.
og_description: Skool, Circle.so, TagMango and AllCoaching compared for Indian educators running paid study groups, with every price from the official site (checked 24 Oct 2026) and an honest answer on when a community platform fits better.
h1: Skool or Circle.so Alternative in India (2026): Running a Paid Study Community, Prices Checked
dek: A fair comparison for Indian educators who want to charge for a study group or community: what Skool and Circle.so charge in dollars, which options price in rupees with UPI checkout, and when a community platform is still the better tool.
cover_alt: Skool or Circle alternative for study communities in India: Skool, Circle.so, TagMango and AllCoaching compared, prices checked on 24 Oct 2026
audience: Indian educators and coaches running or planning a paid study community, cohort or accountability group
intro: The right Skool or Circle.so alternative in India depends on what your members are really paying for: if it is a structured study batch with live classes, tests and notes, sold in rupees with UPI checkout under your own app and domain, AllCoaching fits; if it is a discussion feed with posts, levels and member chat, a community platform such as Skool, Circle.so or India's TagMango fits better.

We are AllCoaching, so read this knowing who wrote it. Every competitor price below comes from that company's own pricing page, with the link and the date we checked it, and we say plainly where another platform fits better than ours. That includes the community feed itself, which is not a feature we list today.

Skool and Circle.so both price in US dollars. Skool charges US$9 a month plus a 10% transaction fee on its Hobby plan, or US$99 a month plus 2.9% on Pro. Circle.so starts at US$89 a month on annual billing, excluding taxes. For an Indian educator, Indian GST and your bank's foreign-currency charges may be added on top.
takeaways: Skool lists Hobby at US$9 a month (US$7.50 on yearly billing) with a 10% transaction fee and Pro at US$99 a month (US$82 yearly) with 2.9%, plus a 7-day free trial (checked 24 Oct 2026).
Circle.so lists Professional at US$89, Business at US$199 and Scale at US$419 a month on annual billing, excluding taxes, with a 14-day trial and no card; custom branded apps are on Circle Plus.
Both price in US dollars; Indian GST and foreign-currency card charges may apply, and neither pricing page lists UPI.
AllCoaching starts at ₹6,999 a year plus a 10% fee on sales (Starter), with Growth ₹12,999 + 7.5%, Pro ₹24,999 + 5%, or monthly at 0% commission from ₹3,999; GST extra, 7-day free trial with no card.
AllCoaching is built for structured study (unlimited live classes, tests, notes, your own Android app, with iOS on Pro); a gamified discussion feed is not among its listed features.
TagMango Basic charges no fixed fee and 10% of sales for up to 200 students, so it costs less than AllCoaching up to about ₹5 lakh of sales, before its ₹24,999 a year custom-domain setup.
For exam aspirants, a weekly rhythm of live classes and tests usually matters more than a leaderboard; for hobby and business groups, a feed may be the product.

sections.h2: The short answer: decide what members pay for
sections.html:
Before you compare platforms, decide what your members are buying. A NEET aspirant paying ₹499 a month usually wants the next live class, a doubt answered and a test that shows progress. A business-skills group may want the conversation itself. The platform follows from that.

{{fig:verdict|Which Skool or Circle alternative to choose in India: structured study batches with live classes and tests, AllCoaching; course plus community in rupees, TagMango; a gamified feed is the product, Skool; a branded community hub, Circle.so|Pick the row that sounds like you. The rest of this guide explains each choice.}}

If you are not sure yet, the next sections show how we compared the options and what each one is good at.

sections.h2: How we compared Skool, Circle.so and Indian alternatives
sections.html:
We compared Skool and Circle.so with two options Indian educators shortlist for paid groups: TagMango and AllCoaching. We looked at six things.

  1. Published price and currency, taken only from each company's own pricing page.
  2. Fee on your sales, because many community platforms take a percentage.
  3. Checkout for Indian members: rupee pricing and UPI, or something to ask about.
  4. What the platform is built around: a discussion feed, or classes, tests and notes.
  5. What you own: your domain, your app listing and your member data.
  6. How you start: trial, card requirement or a call.
Disclosure: AllCoaching publishes this guide. Competitor figures link to their official pages and carry the date we checked them (24 Oct 2026). Prices change; check the source before you decide. If you spot an error, write to contact@allcoaching.in and we will correct it.

sections.h2: Why Indian educators look for a Skool or Circle.so alternative
sections.html:
Skool and Circle.so are well-built community platforms, and for many groups they are the right choice. Indian educators usually start comparing for three reasons.

What Skool and Circle.so do well

Skool combines a community with courses, live calls and gamification, and its plans include "Unlimited members, Unlimited courses, Unlimited videos, Unlimited live calls".[1] Circle.so brings community, courses, events and branded apps together, with the line "Run your entire digital business on Circle".[2] If your members come for discussion, peer support and a sense of belonging, these tools are designed exactly for that.

1. Dollar pricing for rupee members

A study group in India often charges ₹299 to ₹999 a month. Your platform bill is in US dollars, so its rupee cost moves with the exchange rate, your card may add a foreign-currency charge, and Indian GST may apply. On Skool's Hobby plan, the 10% transaction fee also comes on top of the US$9 monthly price.

2. A checkout members can finish

Many aspirants pay by UPI, often from a parent's phone. Neither Skool's nor Circle.so's pricing page lists UPI, and Circle.so's page does not state its transaction fees. Ask both directly. Our guide to the best UPI payment gateway for online courses explains why this decides how many members actually join.

{{q:Is a discussion feed still useful for a study group?|Yes, as support around the main work. Members asking each other questions and sharing a good mock score build real community. What usually does not carry an exam group on its own is a feed where points reward posting, not learning. Keep the conversation, but anchor the group in live classes and tests.}}

3. Structure matters more than status for exam groups

For NEET, JEE, SSC or UPSC aspirants, the thing that keeps them going for months is usually a fixed weekly rhythm: a live class, a place to clear doubts, and a test that answers "am I improving?" That is closer to a coaching batch than to a social feed. Our guide on reducing student dropout in online coaching covers how to build that rhythm.

{{fig:before-after|Before and after: a dollar community bill, a leaderboard that rewards posting, doubts lost in the feed and tests on Google Forms, compared with one academy login with live classes, tests, notes, your own app and UPI checkout|Whatever you choose, the goal is the same: members who show up every week and can see their progress.}}

sections.h2: 4 options for a paid study community in India, compared fairly
sections.html:
Here is each option as its own company describes it, with the published price, what to check, and who it suits best. Skool and Circle.so are included as options to stay on, because for some groups they are the right answer.

Our platform · disclosure

1. AllCoaching

Good at
An academy you build yourself, like Shopify for coaching: sign up, choose a plan, upload your course, connect your domain and start selling. For a study group that means unlimited live classes (YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in room), tests, PDF notes and recorded lessons under your own website and Android app (iOS app on Pro), with UPI or card checkout and automatic Razorpay payouts.
Published price
Starter ₹6,999/yr + 10% on sales, Growth ₹12,999/yr + 7.5%, Pro ₹24,999/yr + 5%, or monthly at 0% commission from ₹3,999; GST extra. Pricing[4]
Free trial
7 days, no card needed.
Check
A gamified discussion feed with posts, levels and leaderboards is not among AllCoaching's listed features. If that feed is your product, a community platform fits better; many educators pair a structured batch with a WhatsApp group for chat.
Best for
Exam and skill educators selling a study batch with a weekly rhythm of classes and tests.

2. TagMango

Good at
Courses, community and automation for coaches, with an AI add-on stack and optional branded apps; its page promises a custom domain live "24 hours from onboarding".
Published price
Basic: no fixed fee + 10% commission (up to 200 students); Pro ₹5,000/month + 5.5%; Advanced ₹15,000/month + 3.5%; Ultimate ₹30,000/month with zero commission (gateway charge from 1.9%). A custom domain needs the Freedom Setup at ₹24,999/yr; branded apps are a ₹74,999 setup. All + GST.[3]
Free trial
Not stated; the page offers "Book a Call".
Check
The 200-student cap on Basic, and the cost of the domain and app add-ons you need.
Best for
Coaches who want course and community together, priced in rupees, and are comfortable starting with a call.

3. Stay on Skool

Good at
Community with courses, live calls and gamification, with unlimited members, courses, videos and live calls on its plans.
Published price
Hobby US$9/month (US$7.50 on yearly billing) + 10% transaction fee; Pro US$99/month (US$82 yearly) + 2.9%. Prices in US dollars.[1]
Free trial
14 days.
Check
Whether Indian members can pay by UPI, and whether GST applies to your bill.
Best for
Groups where the conversation and member engagement are the product.

4. Stay on Circle.so

Good at
Community, courses, events and branded apps in one platform; its Professional plan includes Circle's own iOS, Android and desktop apps.
Published price
Professional US$89, Business US$199, Scale US$419 a month on annual billing, excluding taxes; Circle Plus custom. Custom branded apps are on Circle Plus.[2]
Free trial
14 days, no credit card required.
Check
Transaction and payment fees, which the pricing page does not state, and UPI for Indian members.
Best for
Larger communities and membership businesses that want a polished hub with events.

sections.h2: What a paid study group costs as it grows
sections.html:
Most community platforms combine a plan price with a percentage, so the total depends on your sales. The chart adds each published rupee plan to its published fee at five sales levels and picks the lowest-cost plan at each level. Skool and Circle.so are not on the chart because they price in US dollars, and we do not convert currencies.

{{fig:cost|Total yearly cost at ₹50,000 to ₹10 lakh of sales from published rupee prices for AllCoaching, TagMango, and TagMango with its custom-domain setup|Before GST. TagMango is shown twice: plans only, and with the ₹24,999 a year Freedom Setup it requires for a custom domain.}} {{cost_table}}

The honest reading: on plan price and commission alone, TagMango Basic costs less than AllCoaching up to about ₹5 lakh of sales a year, because it has no fixed fee; note that Basic is capped at 200 students. Above about ₹5 lakh, AllCoaching Pro costs less. If you want your group on your own domain, TagMango's Freedom Setup adds ₹24,999 a year, and at that point AllCoaching costs less at every level in the chart.

For the dollar platforms, compare in their own terms. A group of 100 members paying ₹499 a month brings in about ₹50,000 a month (illustrative). On Skool Hobby, the 10% fee on that is the same rate as AllCoaching Starter, plus US$9 a month for the plan; on Skool Pro the fee drops to 2.9% and the plan rises to US$99 a month. Use our plan finder to run your own rupee numbers.

sections.h2: Which option fits your study community
sections.html:
Exam accountability group (NEET, JEE, SSC, banking, UPSC)

Build the group as a batch: a fixed weekly live class, a doubt session and a test every week or two. AllCoaching fits this, with your own app so members open your name every day. See how to run live classes on mobile apps and how to create mock tests online.

Skill cohort without an exam date (spoken English, coding, trading, yoga)

Progress is continuous, so a rolling cohort with regular live sessions works well. Price it in rupees and keep the checkout to one tap. See teaching spoken English online and teaching yoga online.

Coach whose members come for the conversation

If discussion, introductions and peer support are what members value most, choose a community platform: TagMango if you want rupee pricing, Skool or Circle.so if your members are global.

Large membership business with events

Circle.so's higher plans are built for this. Compare its annual cost with the value of a branded app and rupee checkout for your Indian members.

sections.h2: How to move a paid community without losing members
sections.html:
The safe way to move is to run both side by side. Members who paid keep their current access until their period ends; new members join your new academy.

{{fig:switch|Four steps to move a paid study community from Skool or Circle.so: build your academy, run both side by side, send new members to your academy, close the old plan at renewal|Nobody loses access, and nobody pays twice.}} {{steps}}

The full checklist, including messages to send members, is in how to switch coaching apps without losing students.

items: Start the 7-day trial, connect your domain, set up your first batch and schedule its live classes.
Keep current members on Skool or Circle.so until their paid period ends, so nobody loses access.
Send new members to your academy
Share your own website and app link with rupee pricing and UPI checkout in every post, video and WhatsApp message.
Export records and close the old plan
Download member and payment records, then let the old plan end at renewal.

faq: What is a good Skool or Circle.so alternative for a paid study community in India?

It depends on what members pay for. AllCoaching fits a structured study batch with live classes, tests and notes, sold in rupees with UPI checkout under your own app and domain, from ₹6,999 a year plus a fee on sales. TagMango fits course plus community in rupees, and Skool or Circle.so fit groups where the discussion feed is the product.
How much do Skool and Circle.so cost in India?

Skool lists Hobby at US$9 a month with a 10% transaction fee and Pro at US$99 a month with 2.9%. Circle.so lists Professional at US$89, Business at US$199 and Scale at US$419 a month on annual billing, excluding taxes (checked 24 Oct 2026). Prices are in US dollars, so Indian GST and foreign-currency card charges may apply.
Does Skool take a fee on sales?
Yes. Skool's pricing page lists a 10% transaction fee on Hobby and 2.9% on Pro. Circle.so's pricing page does not state a transaction fee, so ask Circle directly.
Can Indian members pay by UPI on Skool or Circle.so?
Neither pricing page lists UPI as a payment method (checked 24 Oct 2026). Ask each platform before you rely on it for Indian members.
Does AllCoaching have a community feed like Skool?

A gamified discussion feed is not among AllCoaching's listed features. AllCoaching is built around structured study: unlimited live classes, tests, notes and recorded lessons in your own app. If a feed is your product, a community platform fits better.
Can I run live classes and a paid group in one app?

Yes. Every AllCoaching plan includes unlimited live classes through YouTube Live, Zoom or the built-in live room, inside your own Android app (iOS app on Pro), alongside tests and notes for the same batch.
Do I need my own audience before starting a paid study group?

Mostly yes. Members usually come from your YouTube, Instagram, Telegram or WhatsApp following. AllCoaching also lists your courses on the AllCoaching marketplace app, which helps discovery, but your own channels remain the main source.
How do I move my community without losing members?
Build your new academy, keep current members on the old platform until their paid period ends, send new members to your own website and app, then export records and let the old plan end at renewal.
